definitions.explanation: A broad collection of knowledge on various random topics, not specialized in any particular field. Often valued in Japanese quiz culture and casual conversation.

examples.japanese: {雑学|ざつがく}に{詳|くわ}しい。
テレビの{雑学|ざつがく}クイズが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like trivia quizzes on TV.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{雑学|ざつがく}の{知識|ちしき}が{豊富|ほうふ}で、{話|はなし}をしていて{飽|あ}きない。
examples.english: He has such a wealth of trivial knowledge that you never get bored talking to him.

notes:
USAGE: {雑学|ざつがく} refers to knowledge on a wide range of miscellaneous topics rather than deep expertise in one area. It carries a positive nuance — someone with lots of {雑学|ざつがく} is considered interesting and well-rounded.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雑学|ざつがく}クイズ: trivia quiz
- {雑学|ざつがく}の{知識|ちしき}: trivia knowledge
- {雑学|ざつがく}に{詳|くわ}しい: knowledgeable about trivia
- {雑学|ざつがく}{王|おう}: trivia king

The word is a compound of {雑|ざつ} (miscellaneous) and {学|がく} (learning). Not to be confused with {雑|ざつ} used alone, which has a negative connotation of being sloppy.
